title: Chronological realignment backfill coordinator for Console analytics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a safe, idempotent coordinator service to run time-windowed backfills that realign chronological ordering across multiple event partitions and schema versions for Console usage analytics. Current ad-hoc replays cause subtle ordering regressions in per-route latency/cost aggregations and double-counting when downstream transforms change. The coordinator should: (1) compute deterministic replay windows, (2) emit replay markers and watermarks, (3) orchestrate per-partition workers with causal ordering guarantees, and (4) provide dry-run / validation and retry semantics to avoid permanent metric corruption.
background: Console dashboards aggregate token-level and request-level metrics derived from the eventstream. We introduced a schema change to the route attribution transform last quarter; subsequent reprocess runs produced duplicated cost attributions for ~3% of routes due to non-deterministic replay ordering across partitions. Existing replay tooling (ad-hoc Spark jobs and a simple replayer) lacks: clear windowing, idempotency tokens, schema evolution adapters, and an audit trail tied to Console rollouts.
proposed_solution: Build a Chronological Realignment Backfill Coordinator (CRBC) service that:
proposed_solution_points: Determine canonical time axes using event timestamps plus synthetic watermarks for late-arriving events
Slice backfill into deterministic 'alignment windows' (e.g., 1-hour aligned windows with overlap padding), and compute partition assignments
Attach ephemeral idempotency keys and lineage headers to replayed records to enable downstream deduplication
Provide schema adapters that can translate legacy fields into current transform inputs during replay
Expose dry-run mode that computes expected diffs (row counts, cost deltas) and surfaces them in a preflight report
Record an immutable audit artifact per backfill run: parameters, hashes of input ranges, and generated watermarks
Integrate with existing reprocess queueing and use dedicated low-priority worker pools to avoid impacting live ingestion
acceptance_criteria: Run a controlled backfill for a 3-day window against a staging copy of analytics and show zero duplicates after idempotent dedupe (end-to-end test)
Dry-run report accurately predicts the sign and magnitude of changes for >90% of sampled routes compared to full replay
Backfill runs include an audit artifact accessible from Console UI and a link to the run in the reprocess dashboard
No measurable increase in tail latency for live ingestion when dedicated worker pools are enabled
Automated rollforward/rollback plan defined and verified in chaos testing
tasks: Design alignment-window algorithm and publish spec (owner: Lina)
Implement coordinator API (start/stop/status/dry-run) with run metadata persistence (owner: Backend team)
Wire idempotency/header plumbing into replay producer library (owner: Data infra)
Create schema-adapter layer and one adapter for the route-attribution transform (owner: Applied ML)
Add preflight diff generator and a lightweight simulator that samples inputs (owner: Analytics)
Build audit artifact store and Console integration to surface runs (owner: Console-UX)
Run staging backfill and validate acceptance criteria, iterate on edge cases (owner: SRE)
Write runbooks for operator and post-mortem checklist (owner: Reliability)
Add telemetry (run duration, reprocessed events, dropped/duplicate counts) and SLOs for backfill jobs (owner: Observability)
Coordinate production cutover and communicate to stakeholders (owner: PM)
Retrospective and follow-up tickets for optimizations (owner: PM)
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy CRBC and schema adapters to staging. 2) Run a dry-run for a non-overlapping 72-hour window and verify simulated diffs. 3) Run a small production pilot (1-day) targeting low-traffic customers using dedicated low-priority workers. 4) Expand to wider windows after validation and monitoring. 5) After successful run, mark audit artifact and enable automatic dedupe in downstream joins. All runs require a preflight approval and a rollback key. Communication plan includes an announcement to Console owners, docs, and a dashboard link.
testing_plan: Unit tests for alignment math, property tests for idempotency keys, integration tests using staging event copies, end-to-end validation against a reference implementation (golden dataset), and chaos tests that simulate late arrivals and partition reassignment. Include synthetic tests for schema migrations.
notes: We considered adapting the existing replayer but determined it lacks deterministic windowing and robust dedupe headers; rewriting as a coordinator service provides clear separation of concerns and smaller blast radius. Key risk: ensuring downstream transforms actually honor idempotency headers — we will add lightweight verification hooks and failure metrics.
risks_mitigation: Downstream transforms ignore idempotency headers => mitigation: add dedupe-sidecar that checks lineage hashes and emits alerts
Late-arriving events outside padding windows => mitigation: use conservative overlap and re-run small tail backfills
Schema adapter bugs => mitigation: require adapter unit tests and golden-file validation
